sn35.32:1.1: “Bhikkhus, I will teach you the way that is suitable for uprooting all conceivings.
sn35.32:1.3: “And what, bhikkhus, is the way that is suitable for uprooting all conceivings?
sn35.32:2.2: is the eye permanent or impermanent?”—
sn35.32:4.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”—
sn35.32:6.1: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.32:6.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”—
sn35.32:10.1: Is any feeling that arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant—permanent or impermanent?…
sn35.32:22.1: Is any feeling that arises with mind-contact as condition permanent or impermanent?”—
sn35.32:24.1: “Is what is impermanent suffering or happiness?”—
sn35.32:26.1: “Is what is impermanent, suffering, and subject to change fit to be regarded thus:
sn35.32:26.2: ‘This is mine, this I am, this is my self’?”—
sn35.32:28.1: “Seeing thus, bhikkhus, the instructed noble disciple experiences revulsion towards the eye, towards forms, towards eye-consciousness, towards eye-contact,
sn35.32:28.2: towards whatever feeling arises with eye-contact as condition—whether pleasant or painful or neither-painful-nor-pleasant.
sn35.32:28.3: He experiences revulsion towards the ear …
sn35.32:28.5: towards whatever feeling arises with mind-contact as condition….
sn35.32:28.6: Experiencing revulsion, he becomes dispassionate. Through dispassion his mind is liberated. When it is liberated there comes the knowledge: ‘It’s liberated.’
sn35.32:28.7: He understands: ‘Destroyed is birth, the holy life has been lived, what had to be done has been done, there is no more for this state of being.’
sn35.32:28.8: “This, bhikkhus, is the way that is suitable for uprooting all conceivings.”
